meta.title: Shark · Commercial Command Center
meta.subtitle: A quarter of continuous collection, extrapolated from the measured snapshot
meta.subject: shark

disclosure.headline: The figures on these screens are extrapolated, not measured.
disclosure.body: Every Sonos lane we hold today is a single capture. This dashboard answers what a quarter of continuous collection would look like: the measured snapshot is used as an anchor and a 13-week daily panel is simulated around it, with retail-calendar seasonality, promotional cycles, stock episodes and competitive response. Levels are pinned to what was measured; shapes are modelled. Nothing here should be read as a reported result.

anchors.measured: MEASURED: Amazon carriage, shelf price and promotions for every tracked listing; Amazon shelf share per brand; the listing lead time per brand; six months of audited price and availability history.
anchors.pins: EXTRAPOLATED FROM IT: carriage and price at the four retailers beyond Amazon; shelf share per retailer per term; the metro delivery spread. Those lanes are modelled around the measured anchors on the same machinery this dashboard uses everywhere else — read them as the shape a quarter would take, not as observations.

anchors.measured: Street price, list price, discount rate and offer count for 11 Amazon listings across 4 brands, monthly 2026-01 to 2026-06
anchors.pins: Every daily price ladder is bounded by its brand's measured discount rate — Shark 15.6%, Dyson 0.1%, Tineco 4.1%, LG 18.2%.

anchors.measured: PDP shelf price for 11 models across 1 retailers, captured 2026-08-15
anchors.pins: Each simulated ladder is scaled to land on the captured price at the capture date.

anchors.measured: 24 promotion verbatims across 11 product pages, each located and outlined in the captured image
anchors.pins: The mechanic set, the per-retailer mix, and every promotion type shown.
Carried and not-carried cells are held fixed; only 'not readable' cells are extrapolated.

anchors.measured: Share of days in the last audited month with a buyable Amazon offer — Shark 95.6%, Dyson 100%, Tineco 93.3%, LG 33.4%
anchors.pins: The target in-stock rate each simulated episode series is drawn against.

anchors.measured: 11 delivery-promise readings across 11 models, 1 retailers and 0 cities
anchors.pins: Week-one lead time for every model-retailer-city triple that was captured.

anchors.measured: Share of the result grid per retailer per search term across 1 terms, 3 passes
anchors.pins: The level each daily shelf-share series reverts to.

anchors.measured: Share of the AI answer across 3 engines by funnel stage. Any engine shown on the dashboard beyond those is modelled off their mean and is a column of illustration, not a measurement.
anchors.pins: The per-engine and per-stage level each daily series reverts to, for the engines that were captured.

anchors.measured: Amazon star rating weighted by rating count, and monthly aspect scores from captured reviews across 8 aspects
anchors.pins: Rating levels, and every aspect month that had a real reading is passed through untouched.

anchors.measured: Monthly visits, US share, bounce rate, pages per visit, visit duration, leading channel and country mix for 4 of 4 brand domains — sharkclean.com 0.5M, dyson.com 4.3M, tineco.com 1.0M, lg.com 36.2M. dyson.com and lg.com are whole-domain reads: real, but covering more than this category, and labelled that way wherever they appear.
anchors.pins: The session level for each measured brand, its bounce, pages per visit and duration, its leading channel share, and its country mix. NOT the day-to-day shape — the profile publishes a monthly figure, so the movement across the quarter is still modelled — not the rest of the channel split, which sits behind a subscription, not add-to-cart, which is published nowhere, and not the retail product-page split, which is modelled from shelf presence and retailer weight.

disclosure.paletteNote: Shark’s own navy sits too close to Dyson’s for a categorical slot, and the pair a reader most needs to separate here is the subject against Dyson.

promoTypes.label: Price discount
promoTypes.note: Straight markdown off the list price. Modelled as fully brand-funded through price protection — the assumption a commercial team is most likely to want to change.

promoTypes.label: Card offer
promoTypes.note: Retailer card instant offer — $50 off on approval, seen on every Amazon listing in the capture.

promoTypes.label: Protection plan
promoTypes.note: Retailer-sold cover. Adds to what the shopper pays rather than reducing it.

promoTypes.label: Buy now, pay later
promoTypes.note: Pay in 4 / Affirm. Cost is the platform fee.

promoTypes.label: Accessory bundle
promoTypes.note: Extra tools, filters or a spare battery attached below the sum of the parts.

promoTypes.label: Gift card back
promoTypes.note: Store credit returned on purchase — a mass-retail mechanic that keeps the spend in the retailer.

promoTypes.label: Trade-in
promoTypes.note: Credit for an old machine returned at purchase.

promoTypes.label: Clearance
promoTypes.note: End-of-line markdown to clear a superseded model.

promoTypes.label: Free delivery
promoTypes.note: Shipping absorbed by the retailer or the brand.

promoFamilies.label: Finance
promoFamilies.note: Spreads or offsets the payment on approval.

promoFamilies.label: Attached value
promoFamilies.note: Something extra at no or low cost.

overview.text: Over the 13 weeks Shark holds 39.4% of the AI answer — second of the 4 — against 29.8% of the retail shelf, first of the 4. The brand is being recommended far more often than it is being seen on a result grid.
Price discipline is intact: Shark transacts at 77.4% of MSRP, third of the 4, while the set as a whole runs at 80.1%.
Share of category traffic sits at 10.9%, second of the 3, and moved -1.8pp between the open and the close of the quarter.
In-stock rate of 93.7% is second of the 4; 66 separate out-of-stock episodes cost 166 listing-days across the carried estate, 24 of them opening within five days of a discount deeper than 14%.

traffic.text: sharkclean.com drew 462.3k visits worldwide last month, 75% of them from the United States — 346.7k US visits, measured rather than modelled. The day-to-day shape across the quarter is still modelled; the level is not.

Shark takes 10.9% of the tracked brand-site visits, second of the 3; Dyson is the nearest of the rest on 80.8%. LG is excluded: its own domain is not a fair proxy for the product line, so counting it would divide by a business this category is only a corner of. The comparison is domain against domain, not product line against product line — Dyson carries several categories on the same site.
Assistant referrals grew from 503 to 869 sessions a day across the quarter — a 72.7% rise, the fastest-growing channel in the mix.
Paid search carries 15.5% of Shark sessions, the second-least paid-dependent of the 3; Tineco runs the most paid-dependent mix at 22.6%.

ai.text: Shark is second of the 4 on share of the AI answer at 39.4%.
Presence is uneven by engine: Perplexity returns Shark in 44.3% of answers against 35.7% on Gemini — a 8.6-point spread on the same prompt set.
The strongest funnel position is evaluation at 46.3%, the weakest consideration at 31.6%.

shelf.text: Shelf share of 29.8% puts Shark first of the 4; Dyson is the nearest of the rest on 12.2%.
Presence concentrates where the intent is specific — "vacuum for pet hair" returns Shark in 38.4% of the grid, against 24% on the weakest term.
19.8% of Shark shelf presence is paid — the most paid-reliant of the 4. Shark buys its way onto the grid at 19.8%, which is why Shark share moves against it in event weeks.
Amazon reads thinnest for Shark at 20% of the grid, against 38.7% at Walmart — a 18.7-point gap between the brand's best and worst shelf.

distribution.text: Shark occupies 30 of 35 possible model-by-retailer cells — 79.5% weighted for the days each listing was actually live, first of the 4.
9 listings changed state inside the quarter: 2 dropped, 5 appeared, 2 lapsed and returned.
Buy-box ownership averages 94.6% on the marketplaces, first of the 4 — every point lost is a sale credited to a reseller at a price the brand did not set.

availability.text: In-stock rate of 93.7% is second of the 4; 66 out-of-stock episodes cost 166 listing-days over the quarter.
24 of those 66 episodes opened within five days of a discount deeper than 14% — the promotion cleared the shelf faster than replenishment refilled it.

delivery.text: The Shark delivery promise averages 5.8 days — the second-fastest of the 4, against 5.6 days for Dyson, the fastest of the rest.
The promise is not national: Miami, FL waits 6.4 days against 5.1 in New York, NY — a 1.3-day spread on the same catalogue.

pricing.text: Shark realises 77.4% of MSRP across the quarter, third of the 4 — the category runs 80.1% and LG clears at 58.2%.
Clean & Empty Stick carries the widest cross-retailer spread at $123.21 on average and $143.23 at its widest — a shopper comparing two tabs sees two different brands.
29 listings traded below the 80% floor for 1462 days in total, worst at 31.3% under.

promotions.text: Shark runs a price promotion on 38% of carried listing-days — the third-least promoted of the 4. LG is on promotion 43.8% of the time.
When Shark does promote it goes 21.9% deep against a category mean of 14.3% — the deepest of the 4 on discount depth.
56.2% of Shark price events open inside a retail-calendar window, spread across 5 retailers; 121 episodic events ran in the quarter at a mean 10.5 days each.
The mechanic doing most of the work is free delivery at 30.5% of Shark promotional days.

tco.text: Attach-weighted, the shelf price understates what a Shark buyer actually pays by 0.4% — the narrowest of the 4. Tineco shows a 1.3% gap, 3.2x wider, so a shelf-price comparison against it is not a like-for-like read.
Detect Pro Auto-Empty at Target carries the widest single gap: $396.59 on the shelf against $384.25 attach-weighted, of which $111.11 is funded by the brand rather than the retailer.

15 of 28 Shark listings carry three or more simultaneous mechanics. The more mechanics on a page, the less the shelf price says about the transaction — and the harder a competitor's headline price is to read straight.

voice.text: Shark rates 4.21★, first of the 4; Shark leads on 4.21★.
Review velocity of 8.8k over the quarter is first of the 4 — a smaller base to defend the rating with.
